title: Learning Martial Arts Motion Skills for Animating Opponents in VR Sparring Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.23825v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Animating virtual opponents is an important yet challenging task in game development. In martial arts games, opponent motions must not only be physically plausible but also exhibit appropriate technique, timing, transitions, and target-directed intent. Traditional game animations often rely on handcrafted clips, state machine transitions, and procedural adjustments, which can be labor-intensive and may limit the behavioral diversity of non-player characters. This paper presents a martial arts motion skills learning framework for character animation in virtual sparring games. Inspired by Tang Soo Do, we collected a martial arts motion capture dataset containing isolated attacking and defending techniques, technique combinations and transitions, and contextual sparring variations. We first pretrained a reusable repertoire of martial arts motion skills from the captured data using reinforcement learning (RL) with adversarial style rewards

translated_title: 面向VR对打游戏中对手动画的武术动作技能学习
translated_abstract: 在游戏开发中，为虚拟对手制作动画是一项重要且具有挑战性的任务。在武术游戏中，对手的动作不仅要符合物理合理性，还应展现出恰当的技巧、时机、动作转换以及针对目标的意图。传统游戏动画通常依赖手工制作的动作片段、状态机转换和程序化调整，这些方法不仅劳动强度大，还可能限制非玩家角色行为的多样性。本文提出了一种面向虚拟对打游戏中角色动画的武术动作技能学习框架。受唐手道（Tang Soo Do）启发，我们收集了一个武术动作捕捉数据集，其中包含独立的攻防技术、技术组合与转换，以及情境化的对打变化。我们首先利用带有对抗性风格奖励的强化学习（RL）从捕捉的数据中预训练出一套可复用的武术动作技能库。
tldr: 本文提出一个受唐手道启发的武术动作技能学习框架，利用动作捕捉数据集和带对抗性风格奖励的强化学习预训练出可复用的武术技能库，用于生成VR对打游戏中逼真且具有战术意图的虚拟对手动画。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a martial arts motion skills learning framework inspired by Tang Soo Do, which pretrains a reusable repertoire of martial arts motion skills from a motion capture dataset using reinforcement learning with adversarial style rewards, enabling realistic and tactically intentional virtual opponent animation in VR sparring games.
